english.title: Arrange / facilitate the commission of child sex offence - rape / assault by penetration of child under 13
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally arranged or facilitated an act which you

(A)_[intended to do]_
(B)_[intended another person to do]_
(C)_[believed another person would do]_

in any part of the world, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), which would involve the commission of an offence under section

(D)_[5 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 of rape of a child under 13]_
(E)_[6 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 of sexual assault of a child under 13 by penetration]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 14 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Prior to 28th June 2022, section 14 only covered the commission of an offence under sections 9 to 13 of the Act, but now covers the commission of offences under sections 5 to 13. This offence wording covers sections 5 and 6 offences only; for offences committed before 28th June, see H5719.
(ii) See further offence wordings involving the commission of an offence under section 7 (H100737), sections 8, 9 or 10 (penetration: section 8 - H100738; section 9 or 10 - H100739; no penetration: section 8 - 10 H100740), sections 11 or 12: H100741; section 13: H100742.
(iii) For attempt of this offence see H100736.
(iv) Provided the victim was under 16, an act done by a person in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which constituted an offence under the law in force in that country or territory, and would constitute a sexual offence to which this section applies if it had been done in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland, constitutes that sexual offence under the law of that part of the United Kingdom, and provided that person was on 01/09/1997, or who has since become a British citizen or resident in the United Kingdom he or she may have proceedings brought against them in the United Kingdom, section 72.
(v) A person convicted of this offence who was aged 18 or over or sentenced in respect of this offence to at least twelve months imprisonment is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act (Schedule 3, paragraph 23).
